angle: DL/EDGE: pass-rush-drill get-off burst and Run-the-Hoop bend (Hoop G), year-standardized, against NFL get-off, NFL first-second burst, NFL bend and career pressure rate; baseline = log pick + weight + EDGE share + NGS athleticism + official 10-yd split + 3-cone, leave-one-class-out; decision use = day-3 tiebreaker when no-tracking forecasts are within 0.5 pressure-rate points
metric_name: Hoop G: the most sideways g a lineman holds for half a second on the Run-the-Hoop figure-eight, z within Combine year (contrast: rush-drill burst, yards in the first second of the pass-rush drill)
headline_number: Out of class (n=77): Hoop G +1.8 pressures per 450-rush season per sd [0.2, 3.4], shuffle p=0.02, 33% of draws above the 2.25 action margin, flat in 2025; slope 1.5-2.0 across 7 sensitivity settings. Burst -0.5 [-2.3, 1.3], TOST p=0.06. Day-3 ties (125 pairs, 47 rushers): Hoop G right 56% [43, 69] vs break-even 37% and earlier pick 50%; net +2.6 pressures per decision [0.1, 5.1], p=0.03; nested back-test (tie width re-chosen out of class) 52% vs earlier pick 61%, both +3.4.
what_changed_from_previous: Revision of round 18 cand_1 (DL Hoop G, 8.07), applying the round-18 judges' transferable top_changes. (1) Coach-repeatable one-sentence Hoop G definition; physics derivation and the snap-level mechanism paragraph cut to one sentence; single unit (pressures per 450-rush season) throughout. (2) All reliability numbers (hoop lap, burst rep, NFL bend, NFL burst, NGS get-off, pressure rate season-to-season) in one table (Table 1). (3) Decision arithmetic table: hit rate, error rate with interval, gain-when-right/loss-when-wrong, break-even hit rate 37%, net gain with rusher-clustered permutation p, per-class record for Hoop G and earlier pick, and a nested leave-one-class-out back-test that re-chooses the tie width on the other two classes, reported against the pick-only tiebreaker (it does not beat pick on hit rate: 52% vs 61%). Pick-gap split explains why ties are defined by forecast, not pick gap. (4) Sensitivity table rerunning the whole pipeline for shrinkage prior x0.5/x2, 20+/50+ rush minimum, tie width 0.25/1.0. (5) 2026 board widened to the 2024 and 2025 day-3 shortlists: 5 Go (Cedric Johnson, Javon Solomon, Warren Brinson, Austin Booker, Jack Sawyer), 3 No-go, 3 Hold, 7 auditions, each with the 2026 rate that flips the call, decision date after Week 18 of 2026; new board figure with 90% intervals, distinct marker shapes (Go blue circle, Hold orange square, No-go vermillion cross). (6) Fig 2 is now six small-multiple laps with Hoop G and speed printed and a median-runner ghost lap; transfer figure replaced by the reliability table; break-even line and back-test row added to the tie figure. (7) verify.py now recomputes the shrunk rates from raw counts, the per-class records, pick-gap split, break-even and the nested back-test. 4 figures + 4 tables, ~1,800 words.
open_risks: Nested back-test: with the tie width chosen out of class, earlier pick is right more often than Hoop G (61% vs 52%) and the per-decision gains are equal (+3.4); the rule's edge over draft order is not robust
Tie-rule hit rate unproven (56%, p=0.20); the significant net gain (p=0.03) shrinks to +1.6 without the five biggest wins
Hoop G was selected after earlier rounds screened drill measures on these same classes; 2026 is the first clean test (power 43% for one class)
Out-of-class effect is flat in the 2025 class (-0.02 pts per sd)
Go/No-go calls rest on NFL pressure vs forecast within a Hoop G shortlist, so they mostly reflect NFL performance; board intervals are wide (shrunk-rate uncertainty only, forecast error not included)
No-tracking baseline overfits (held-out R2 -0.02 vs 0.10 for pick+role)
